thread.title: Nasdaq Trims Loss, While Dow Jones Sends Message | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Nasdaq Trims Loss, While Dow Jones Sends Message | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Bears delivered some heavy damage Tuesday morning, whacking the Nasdaq down to a fresh low before the tech-leaning index could recover. The blue-chip Dow Jones industrial average, large-cap S&P 500 and small-cap S&P 600 held above their Oct. 29 lows.
X Volume stepped up from the same time in the previous session as the Nasdaq chalked up a 0.7% loss after being down as much as 2.8%. The Dow Jones industrial average fell 1.6%; the S&P 500, 1.1%; and the S&P 600, 0.7%.
In vicious circumstances, investors naturally look around for a cause. That's a futile approach and ultimately a distraction. Price action, volume and the stock charts will tell the individual investor all they need to know in order to act.
For now, the stock charts are saying conditions are ugly and raising cash is prudent.
Investors might take a close look at the Dow because it provides a concise basis of comparison. The tech stocks in the Dow are suffering. Apple ( AAPL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) are down 7% and 5.5% so far this week. Cisco ( CSCO ) is off 3%. Intel ( INTC ) and IBM ( IBM ) are down 2% and 3%, respectively.
Stocks in the Dow Jones industrials that have behaved well enough to be too extended to buy include Coca-Cola ( KO ), Verizon Communications ( VZ ) and Merck ( MRK ).
Dow stocks consolidating in bases include American Express ( AXP ) and Pfizer ( PFE ). Two in the 5% buy zone include Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) and McDonald's ( MCD ). The message the Dow is sending is to put the above four on a watch list.
If the market steers north, the stocks that held up under market pressure could be an investor's best bet.
Dividends In Dow Jones Dividend stocks provide another segment of the Dow Jones to consider. IBM's annualized dividend yield is currently 5.2%. Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) offers a 4.1% yield; Verizon, 4%; and Chevron ( CVX ) 3.8%.
Yet overall, the Dow isn't especially attractive in this market. Of the 30 stocks in the Dow, half are below their 200 day lines and only a third are above their 50-day lines.
Among IBD's 197 industry groups, seven were up as the market approached the lunch hour. Gainers included dairy, diversified operations, packaged food, confectionery food, homebuilders, meat and diversified utilities.
The day's biggest losers included department stores, shippers and discount retail.
Coming Up The Group of 20 summit in Argentina on Nov. 30 and Dec. 1 is expected to involve talks between China leader Xi Jinping and President Trump. If the two reach an agreement, bulls say the stock market could deliver a big rally.
Bears, though, aren't expecting much to come out of the meeting.
